# Gazillion Industries

> Gazillion Industries LLC makes audio software: plug-ins for macOS and Windows,
> and one iPad app. Each product does one job, opens with the control you came
> for already on screen, and needs no manual. Six are out.

## Products

- [F(ilter)12](https://gazillionindustries.com/f12.html) — a 12 bit sauce
  filter. $49.
- [DRUGS](https://gazillionindustries.com/drugs.html) — a one-knob character bus
  compressor. Free, or name your own price.
- [SKRUU](https://gazillionindustries.com/skruu.html) — varispeed pitch and
  time stretch. Control pitch and time independently. $29.
- [TRIPLE OG](https://gazillionindustries.com/tripleog.html) — cassette tape
  simulation with a transport you can grab. $29.
- [BEEFY](https://gazillionindustries.com/beefy.html) — a saturation and
  loudness plugin with soft clipping, for drums, 808s, bass and samples. $19.
- [Chordea](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/chordea/id6757318321) — a MIDI chord
  controller for iPad. $9.99 on the App Store.

## BEEFY

A saturation and loudness effect for macOS and Windows, for making sounds
thicker, punchier and more up front. It adds body, squeezes some space out of
the peaks, and brings out harmonics that help a sound feel bigger. Built for
drums, 808s and bass, and just as usable on synths, chopped samples, keys,
guitar and vocals.

- BEEF: the main control. More weight, density and loudness as it goes up
- COOK: tone, from rounder toward a brighter, more bitten edge
- JUICE: input level
- SOFT CLIP: on by default. Rounds off the loudest parts and adds harmonics
  above the low end, so an 808 or bass has more to hear than sub. Handles the
  initial gain staging
- LIMIT: keeps output peaks in check; separate from SOFT CLIP
- Input and output clip lights
- A cartoon panel with two finishes and a cow that reacts to the audio
- Resizable window that remembers its size

Formats: macOS VST3, Audio Unit and standalone (Apple Silicon and Intel);
Windows 64-bit VST3. Activation with the included license key needs an internet
connection once, then it works offline. Price: $19, one-time.

## Reading material

Guides on getting drums and low end to hit, written by the people who make the
plugins.

- [How to make 808s hit harder](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-make-808s-hit-harder/)
  — Tuning, the kick, the envelope, saturation, soft clipping and a mono low end.
- [How to make drums hit harder](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-make-drums-hit-harder/)
  — Samples, the transient, compression attack, soft clipping, saturation and room in the mix.
- [Soft clipping explained](https://gazillionindustries.com/soft-clipping-explained/)
  — What a soft clipper does, how it differs from hard clipping and a limiter, and where to use one.
- [How to saturate drums](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-saturate-drums/)
  — Kick, snare, drum bus and parallel saturation, and how to keep cymbals from turning harsh.
- [Gain staging for beatmakers](https://gazillionindustries.com/gain-staging/)
  — Channel levels, plugin input, buses and the master, plus the common mistakes.
- [How to make your mix louder without clipping](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-make-mix-louder-without-clipping/)
  — Low end, balance, density, soft clipping and a true-peak limiter, plus what streaming does to loud masters.
- [Clipper before limiter](https://gazillionindustries.com/clipper-before-limiter/)
  — Why the clipper goes first, how to set both, and why the true-peak limiter stays last.
- [How loud should a master be](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-loud-should-my-master-be/)
  — LUFS, true peak, what Spotify does to loud masters, and how to choose a level with references.
- [Saturation vs distortion](https://gazillionindustries.com/saturation-vs-distortion/)
  — Saturation, overdrive, distortion and fuzz: what changes, and which one you want.
- [How to use saturation in a mix](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-use-saturation/)
  — Bass, drums, vocals, synths, buses and the master: what saturation is for and how much to use.
- [Parallel saturation](https://gazillionindustries.com/parallel-saturation/)
  — Set it up on a return, drive it hard, filter the burnt copy, and blend it under the dry signal.
- [Tape vs tube saturation](https://gazillionindustries.com/tape-vs-tube-saturation/)
  — Which harmonics each adds, what they do to transients, and which to use where.
- [How to mix the kick and the 808](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-mix-kick-and-808/)
  — Who owns the sub, tuning, sidechain, phase, and using the 808 as the kick.
- [How to distort an 808](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-distort-808s/)
  — Keep the sub clean, distort a high-passed copy, pick the drive, and handle glides.
- [How to make bass audible on phone speakers](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-make-bass-audible-on-phone-speakers/)
  — Harmonics, a mid-bass layer, EQ that helps, and testing on a real phone.
- [How to make bass fatter](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-make-bass-fatter/)
  — Layer a sub and mid-bass, add harmonics, compress for consistency, and make it growl.
- [How to make a snare hit harder](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-make-snare-hit-harder/)
  — Sample and tuning, layers, transients, saturation, soft clipping and a short room.
- [How to make drums sound bigger](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-make-drums-sound-bigger/)
  — Room, sustain, density, weight and width: the half of drum sound that punch doesn't cover.
- [How to make drums cut through the mix](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-make-drums-cut-through-the-mix/)
  — Fix masking, keep transients, add presence, duck busy parts, pan with purpose and tame the reverb.
- [Transient shaper vs saturation](https://gazillionindustries.com/transient-shaper-vs-saturation/)
  — Why they push drums in opposite directions, which one your drums need, and how to use both.
- [How to layer kicks](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-layer-kicks/)
  — Top, body and sub: filter each layer, align the starts, fix phase and glue them into one kick.
- [How to make boom bap drums](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-make-boom-bap-drums/)
  — Tempo, sounds, a starting pattern, swing, drum bus processing and structure.
- [How to make drill 808s](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-make-drill-808s/)
  — Glide, sliding lines that stay in key, distortion that keeps the sub, and room for the kick.
- [How to make a sample sound fuller](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-make-a-sample-sound-fuller/)
  — Clean it first, add harmonics, compress for sustain, support it with a bass layer, and give it room.
- [How to make your beats sound fuller](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-make-beats-sound-fuller/)
  — Cover the frequency range, layer and double, add saturation, width and space.
- [How to use distortion on vocals](https://gazillionindustries.com/distortion-on-vocals/)
  — Saturation for presence, parallel distortion for aggression, and heavy drive as an effect.
- [How to make a synth sound thicker](https://gazillionindustries.com/how-to-make-a-synth-sound-thicker/)
  — Unison, oscillators, a mono sub, chorus, saturation and layering, without the harshness.
- [Drum bus compressor settings](https://gazillionindustries.com/drum-bus-compressor-settings/)
  — attack, release, ratio and threshold on a drum bus, and a starting point.
- All guides: https://gazillionindustries.com/reading-material/

## F(ilter)12

A 12 bit sauce filter for macOS and Windows. AURA is an adaptive correction that
moves with the source and sits a record better without sounding processed. Sample
rate and bit reduction, five filter shapes, eight resonance shapes, a slope that
feeds its own distortion back through itself, auto filter and sidechain.

- AURA adaptive enhancement, and MAX AURA
- Sample rate and bit depth reduction
- Five filter shapes: low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, notch and morph
- Eight resonance shapes that travel with the filter
- Slope that feeds its own distortion back through itself
- Auto filter driven by a clock, with swing
- Sidechain that follows another signal
- Zero latency
- Universal binary, Apple Silicon and Intel
- Works offline

Formats: AU, VST3, standalone. Platform: macOS 10.13 or later, Windows 10 or
later. Price: $49.

## Chordea

A MIDI chord controller for iPad. 22 chord types across all twelve roots, from
basic triads to advanced jazz voicings, with the next chord suggested as you
play. A strum plate spans four octaves and takes multi-touch; auto strum runs
forward, backward or ping-pong, from instant to arpeggio. Full USB MIDI out to
hardware synths, DAWs and other iOS apps.

Platform: iPad, iPadOS 16 or later. Price: $9.99 on the App Store. Sold under the
individual Apple developer account, Anthony Greg Barko, rather than under
Gazillion Industries LLC.

## DRUGS

A one-knob character bus compressor for macOS and Windows. Built for dusty, dense
drums: boom bap, beat tapes, chopped breaks, and the kind of low end that pumps.
Vinyl sim style squash on the drum bus, with one control. Free, or name your own
price.

### What it does

DRUGS is a bus compressor with a single macro control called DOSE. Turning DOSE up
makes a drum bus denser rather than louder — peak level barely moves across the
whole range of the control. It reshapes a break instead of just levelling it, and
brings the room up underneath the hits.

It is aimed at producers working in boom bap, beat tapes, lo-fi hip hop, and the
Los Angeles beat scene tradition — the sound of drums that came off a record
rather than out of a computer.

### How it works

- DOSE moves the transfer curve, the knee, the attack and the release together,
  the way a single hardware macro would.
- There is no threshold and no ratio control, because there is no threshold in
  the model. The gain law is a lookup table, so the local ratio changes
  continuously with input level.
- Auto-makeup is applied after the gain cell, so setting level cannot disturb the
  dynamics.
- Release is adaptive and has no user control. It reacts to the transient in
  front of it: a hit gets the shorter time so the gain recovers inside the gap
  where pump is audible, and sustained material gets the longer one so it holds
  still rather than breathing.
- MIX is dry/wet with zero latency anywhere in the path, so the dry signal is
  sample-aligned with the wet one. Parallel compression does not comb-filter at
  any setting.
- LIMIT is a zero-latency soft ceiling at -0.3 dBFS on the output with a clip
  indicator. It attenuates only and is transparent below about -0.9 dBFS.

### The vinyl sim sound

Vinyl sim is shorthand for a particular kind of squash: dense, slightly crushed
drums with the room pushed up under the hits, the way a break sounds once it has
been through a sampler. DRUGS goes at that sound directly, on the drum bus, with
one knob and no setup.

### It is not an emulation

Nothing in DRUGS was measured from hardware. It was voiced by ear on real
material against one person's memory of a machine. It does not model any specific
device and does not claim to. Every constant that shapes the sound is documented
and marked by where it came from.

### Specifications

- Formats: Audio Unit (AU), VST3, standalone application
- Hosts: Logic Pro, Ableton Live, Reaper, Cubase, Studio One, Bitwig, GarageBand
- Platform: macOS 10.13 or later, Windows 10 or later 64-bit
- Architecture: universal binary, Apple Silicon and Intel
- Latency: zero samples
- No internet connection required, ever
